metadata.title: कोयलीबेड़ा और भानबेडा़ आदिवासी बाज़ार | Adivasis of Kumdgunda and Their Weekly Struggle
metadata.description:
In this episode, we travel to Kumdgunda village in Narayanpur district of Chhattisgarh, where Adivasi communities embark on a grueling 35 km journey on foot every week to reach the Koylibeda weekly market. Carrying their precious forest produce, they make this long and difficult trek through forests and rough terrains to sell minor forest products like tendu leaves, mahua, chironji, and more.

But this journey is not just about trade—it's about survival. After selling their goods, they use the little money earned to buy daily essentials like salt, oil, and rice—things they cannot produce in the village.

This episode shines a light on the invisible labor, resilience, and self-reliance of Adivasi communities, while also questioning the lack of basic infrastructure and access to local markets. Why must a community walk 35 km to meet basic needs in 2025?

Watch this ground report to understand the real India that rarely finds space in mainstream narratives.

#MainBhiBharat #AdivasiLives #TribalVoices #ForestProduce #Chhattisgarh #GroundReport #RuralIndia
